title: Hyde's ciphered superscriptions on letters to John Barwick, Brussels 1659-1660

documents.shelfmark: Printed in Peter Barwick, Vita Johannis Barwick (1721), pp. 358, 360, 389, 396

plaintext.source: Life of Dr. John Barwick (1724) p. 409: the superscriptions are numbers 'signifying nothing, only to puzzle the Enemy'

transcription.source: 1721 Vita, checked against archive.org page scans
transcription.notes: Four superscriptions of 12, 14, 7 and 6 groups, counted from the table in NOTES.

system.summary: Dummy numbers written as superscriptions to mislead interceptors; the Hyde-Barwick key (THE=370) does not decode them.
system.sibling_key: Hyde-Barwick key 1-692 from the 1721 plate, applied: gibberish, and six groups outside its range
system.notes: A stock dummy formula 729 549 856 ... 245 831 recurs across three letters.

prior_solution.where: Editor's footnote, Life of Dr. John Barwick (1724) p. 409

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Located the superscriptions in the 1721 Latin Vita and the key plate facing p. 316.
Transcribed the Hyde-Barwick key (643 entries) and applied it.
Template 'For Mr [name] these' and additive offset tested.
1724 editor states the superscriptions are dummy numbers.

outcome.method_basis: The ciphered superscriptions are deliberate nulls, as the editor of the Life of Dr. John Barwick (1724) p. 409 states; applying the Hyde-Barwick key from the 1721 plate confirms it (gibberish, and numbers outside the key).
outcome.notes: Explained as deliberate nulls; editor's statement plus key test.
